text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Moi launches the Eighth National Development Plan which says it's the goverment's intention to place Kenya in the ranks of the newly-industrialised countries by the year 2020.
- Go-slow by air-traffic controllers enters sixth day; some of the instructors redeployed to man control towers as a contigency measure threaten to join the strike.
- Isiolo town in the North Eastern Province is now a major market point of sophisticated illegal guns which are used in robberies in parts of Central province and Nairobi.
- President Moi announces the formation of three committees to review the salaries of civil servants, police officers and employees of Kenya's five public universities.
- Retired Anglican Bishop Henry Okullu says opposition FORD-Kenya dissident Raila Odinga has lost direction and should not expect backing from the majority of the party supporters.
- Kenya Airways Managing Director Brian Davies denies reports that one of their planes was involved in a mid-air near collision with another airline on Wednesday.
- Kenya is ready to cooperate with the Ugandan government to completely eradicate cattle rustling along their common borders.

- Joseph Kamotho, secretary-general of the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party, denies that recent meetings held by prominent businessmen and politicians from Central Province were aimed at defending any Kanu politician.
